Q: Fill empty cells with the same value as previous cell in Google Sheet (Array Formula) A:

use:

=INDEX({A:A, IF(A:A="",, VLOOKUP(ROW(B:B), 
 IF(B:B<>"", {ROW(B:B), B:B}), 2))})

Q: Why does changing the return-type of this C function from 'bool' to 'int' add an additional assembler instruction? A:

As you found out yourself, the reason is different calling conventions. But that only matters because you declared the function with external linkage, meaning that the compiler has to assume it can be called from elsewhere and then the status of any caller-handled registers involved is unknown.

If we make the function static then the resulting assembler turns equivalent because then the compiler can now start to make assumptions about how the function is called. You can easiest observe this if you change the function to:

static __attribute__((noinline)) int self_eq (float num)

Without noinline the compiler will simply remove the whole function, but with noinline it now boils down to a single mov eax, 1 with ucomiss removed, no matter if bool or int.

The take-away from this is that static is not just good for private encapsulation/program design but also for performance. In fact well-designed C programs often result in higher performance.

Q: extracting and creating ipk files A:

And for a newer, xz archives:

#!/bin/sh
for f
do
   ar -p $f ./data.tar.xz | tar tvJf -
done

Q: AntD Date picker + formik A:

After a few days debugging it, I found the issue.

I’m migrating a React version, so I had to migrate AntD as well. Our application was using Moment, but in the current AntD version the DatePicker is based on Day.js. When I tried to pass a Moment object to the component, it broke and started behaving weirdly.

I could try to replicate a Moment object, but the real solution was just to install Day.js. After that, everything worked fine. 🙂

Q: How does ldapsearch sortorder work? A:

When using the -S option, the control is not marked as critical. If the server considers that the use is not allowed or not appropriate, it will ignore the control and proceed with the search (as stated in the LDAP RFC). I'm guessing that this is what you are experiencing.

There can be at least 2 reasons for ignoring the control.

  • The user doesn't have permission to use the control. In OpenDJ, the Server Side Control is only usable by authenticated users, not anonymous.
  • There are too many entries to sort (default I think is set to 4000).

-S 'cn' and -S '-cn' worked as expected on my test OpenDJ server with 200 entries, authenticated as a user or as Directory Manager.
